objectives.text: Meet Ysolde Marnhel at _hall_ in __hall_

outcomes.text: Ysolde Marnhel told you how Dagon's Breaches are opened.
Ysolde Marnhel left _hall_ without you.

objectives.text: Find the coven of Dagon's Faithful in __coven_
Slay the coven's Summoner, =summoner_
Take the rite-book from the Summoner's body
Bring the rite-book to Ysolde Marnhel at _hall_ in __hall_

branches.text: The rite-book's clasp would give at a touch. Read it, or keep it shut for Ysolde?

choices.text: Open it and read what the faithful read
Keep it shut, for it is Ysolde's to open

outcomes.text: You read the rite-book before Ysolde did. She paid well for what you remembered, and the Guild heard the seal was broken.
You brought Ysolde the rite-book with its clasp unbroken, and the Mages Guild knows who did.
Ysolde Marnhel gave the coven up for lost, and the rite-book with it.

objectives.text: At a Dagon's Breach's omen, slay the faithful's Summoner before the door opens
Meet Ysolde Marnhel at _hall_ in __hall_

outcomes.text: You broke the faithful's rite before the breach opened, and Ysolde Marnhel paid for it.
Ysolde Marnhel stopped waiting for word of a broken rite.

objectives.text: Close a Dagon's Breach: fell the Warden who holds its door
Tell Ysolde Marnhel at _hall_ in __hall_

outcomes.text: You closed one of Dagon's burning doors, and Ysolde Marnhel means to put your name in her next book.
Ysolde Marnhel stopped waiting for word of a closed door.

objectives.text: Meet Ysolde Marnhel at _hall_ in __hall_
Tell Ysolde where the embers you carried out of the breaches should go

branches.text: Where should the embers you carried out of Dagon's doors go?

choices.text: To the Mages Guild, for study
To the Order of the Hour, Akatosh's own
To the Sigil Broker, who pays best

outcomes.text: The embers went to the Mages Guild for study, and Ysolde Marnhel will write how a door is shut for good.
The embers went to the Order of the Hour, to lie quiet in the vaults of Akatosh's priests.
The embers went to the Sigil Broker, who pays best. The Mages Guild will hear of it.
Ysolde Marnhel left _hall_ without her answer.

objectives.text: Slay three of the covens' gold-lit champions in the Elite Dungeons
Tell Ysolde Marnhel at _hall_ in __hall_ what you saw

outcomes.text: Three of the covens' gold-lit champions fell, and Ysolde Marnhel learned what they guard: the Battlespire's keys.
Ysolde Marnhel stopped waiting for word of the gold-lit champions.

objectives.text: Find the coven's hold in __lair_
Slay the coven lieutenant, =lieutenant_
Take the Weir Key, wrapped in coven-cloth, from the lieutenant's body
Bring the Weir Key to Ysolde Marnhel at _hall_ in __hall_

outcomes.text: =lieutenant_ is dead, and the covens' Weir Key lies in Ysolde Marnhel's keeping until its fate is decided.
The Weir Key went deeper into the covens' keeping, and Ysolde Marnhel stopped waiting.

objectives.text: Meet Ysolde Marnhel at _hall_ in __hall_
Decide the Weir Key's fate: keep it, or let the Order of the Hour seal it away

branches.text: The Guild gives a house one Weir Key. Keep it, or let the Order of the Hour seal it away?

choices.text: Keep it, for a key is meant to be turned
Give it to the Order of the Hour to be sealed

outcomes.text: You kept the Weir Key for your house and took the Guild's fee. A house is given that key only once, and its road leads to the Spire's torn halls.
The Order of the Hour sealed the Weir Key away in Akatosh's keeping, and will remember who gave it.
Ysolde Marnhel stopped waiting for your answer, and the Weir Key stayed in the Guild's vault.

objectives.text: Meet Prior Anselm Vey of the Order of the Hour at _temple_ in __temple_

outcomes.text: Prior Anselm Vey told you of the Hour beneath the Abyss Dungeons, and of its Orrery of Endings.
Prior Anselm Vey left _temple_ without you.

objectives.text: Meet Prior Anselm Vey at _temple_ in __temple_
Choose which power of the Bay you will tell what you find in the Hour
Break an Hour: go down through an Abyss Dungeon, past the Orrery of Endings, and break the Brass Remnant
Return to Prior Anselm Vey at _temple_ in __temple_

branches.text: Which power will you tell what you find in the Hour?

choices.text: Daggerfall's court
Sentinel's court
Wayrest's court
Another power

branches.text: Which other power will you tell?

choices.text: Orsinium's court
The Underking
The Blades

outcomes.text: You told Daggerfall's court what stands in the Hour. Its herald paid for the account, and asked whether the lion's stone turns.
You told Sentinel's court what stands in the Hour. Queen Akorithi's envoy will tell it as a prophecy of the sun.
You told Wayrest's court what stands in the Hour. King Eadwyre's steward sealed your account in the archive.
You told Orsinium's court what stands in the Hour. Gortwog's emissary stopped laughing at the stone with the tusk.
You told the Underking's agents what stands in the Hour. They paid in old coin; the Order of the Hour will remember it.
You told the Blades what stands in the Hour. They paid poorly, and the Emperor will read your account.
Prior Anselm Vey left _temple_, and the Order sent another down to the Hour.

objectives.text: Win a bout in the Arena in Daggerfall (the Herald at the Arena's gate opens the Ladder)

outcomes.text: You drew first blood on the Arena's sand, and the Herald paid the first purse.
The Herald's call went out to other blood.

objectives.text: Win three bouts in the Arena in Daggerfall

outcomes.text: You won three bouts, and the Herald called your name to the crowd.
The crowd found a new name to shout.

objectives.text: Take a star on the Firmament
Have _seer_ read it at _temple_ in __temple_

outcomes.text: You took your first star, and _seer_ drew it on your chart.
_seer_ put your chart away, still blank.

objectives.text: Take three more stars on the Firmament
Have _seer_ read them at _temple_ in __temple_

outcomes.text: You drew a constellation of your own, and _seer_ gave the sky back to you.
_seer_ put your chart away, half drawn.

objectives.text: Set a gem in a socket
Tell _smith_ at _shop_ in __shop_ which stone you set

outcomes.text: You set a stone in your gear, and _smith_ paid for the lesson learned.
_smith_ found someone else to teach.

objectives.text: Reforge a piece at a Mages Guild's Reforge
Tell _smith_ at _shop_ in __shop_ how the Reforge went

outcomes.text: You had a piece tempered again, and _smith_ told you the last of the trade.
_smith_ stopped waiting to hear of the Reforge.

objectives.text: Catch three fish
Gather three plants
Tell _crafter_ at _store_ in __store_ what you found

outcomes.text: _crafter_ heard you can find your own materials, and paid for the proof.
_crafter_ found another apprentice.

objectives.text: Mine ore or stone three times
Chop wood three times
Tell _crafter_ at _store_ in __store_ the work is done

outcomes.text: You fed the forge and the bench, and _crafter_ paid for the heavy work.
_crafter_ gave the heavy work to someone else.

objectives.text: Make a piece of your own at a crafting station
Tell _crafter_ at _store_ in __store_ what you made

outcomes.text: You made a piece with your own hands, and _crafter_ sent you on as a crafter.
_crafter_ stopped waiting for your piece.

objectives.text: Collect the load from _master_ at _inn_ in __inn_
Haul the load to _buyer_ at _yard_ in __yard_

outcomes.text: You hauled the load to _yard_, and the merchant paid the haulage.
_master_ sent the load with someone else.

objectives.text: Collect the load from _seller_ at _yard_ in __yard_
Haul it back to _master_ at _inn_ in __inn_

outcomes.text: You hauled a load there and back, and _master_ called you a carter.
_master_ gave up waiting for the load.

objectives.text: Take a ship out of one port and bring her into another under sail
Return to _master_, the harbormaster, at _tavern_ in __tavern_

outcomes.text: You made port under your own sail, and the harbormaster paid for it.
The harbormaster found another captain.

objectives.text: Take a cargo off a harbormaster's board (at the helm, lying to a quay) and deliver it

outcomes.text: You delivered a cargo, and a bonus from the harbormaster waited at the quay.
The harbormaster's cargoes went to other ships.

objectives.text: Make a ship strike her colors in a fight at sea
Return to _master_, the harbormaster, at _tavern_ in __tavern_

outcomes.text: You made a ship strike her colors, and the harbormaster drank to the coast's new captain.
The harbormaster hired a navy captain instead.

objectives.text: Win a hand of cards at a tavern's table
Tell _regular_ at _inn_ in __inn_ how you won

outcomes.text: You won a hand, and _regular_ staked you for the next table.
_regular_ found a new stranger to play.

objectives.text: Win a game of the King's Gambit
Tell _regular_ at _inn_ in __inn_ how the other king fell

outcomes.text: Their king fell and yours stood, and _regular_ raised a cup to a general.
_regular_ stopped saving you a seat at the board.

objectives.text: Help drive off a raid on a town
Report to _captain_ at _inn_ in __inn_

outcomes.text: You helped drive the raiders off, and the watch paid for your sword.
_captain_ stopped waiting for your report.

objectives.text: See one of your revenants brought to its knees
Be in a town by day: word from the watch will find you there

outcomes.text: A revenant knelt to you, and the watch sent its thanks and its purse.
The watch stopped waiting to hear of a revenant brought to its knees.

objectives.text: Meet Hamid al-Rasheen, a Sentinel packet captain, at _inn_ in __inn_

outcomes.text: Hamid al-Rasheen told you the sailors' tale of Satakal the World-Skin, and of Sethrakul, the skin that still swims.
Hamid al-Rasheen's packet sailed without you.

objectives.text: Sail the packet lanes: make port twice under sail

outcomes.text: You sailed the packet lanes, and Hamid al-Rasheen hailed you in port: the Old Coil is rising.
The sailing season turned, and Hamid al-Rasheen went home to Sentinel without your word.

objectives.text: Slay the Sea Serpent, Sethrakul, when the harbor bells ring for it
Bring word to Hamid al-Rasheen at _inn_ in __inn_

branches.text: What becomes of the Old Coil's blood and scale?

choices.text: Pour its blood into the sea, the sailors' offering to Satakal
Keep its scale

outcomes.text: You gave the Old Coil's blood back to the sea, the sailors' offering to Satakal. Every port will hear whose offering it was.
You kept a scale of the Old Coil's hide, and every port will know who slew it.
The Old Coil went down for the season, and Hamid al-Rasheen sailed home to Sentinel.

objectives.text: Ask a Wyrd Sister at a tavern's door for word from Morwen
Hold a fallen star
Find Morwen of Glenmoril at __glenmoril_ in ____glenmoril_

outcomes.text: You held a fallen star on the Witches' Festival, and Morwen of Glenmoril told you whose thread had bound it.
Morwen of Glenmoril stopped waiting for word of a star.

objectives.text: Find the Sisters of the Bluff at __bluff_ in ____bluff_
Slay the Sisters' Spinner
Slay the three sisters who stand with her
Bring the spindle to Morwen of Glenmoril at __glenmoril_

branches.text: Any alchemist would pay a fortune for a length of starlit thread. Morwen would rather have it whole.

choices.text: Unwind a length to sell, and give her the rest
Give it to her whole

outcomes.text: You sold Morwen of Glenmoril a length of the Spinner's thread at an alchemist's price, and she took the rest without a word.
You brought Morwen of Glenmoril the Spinner's thread whole, and the Glenmoril Witches will remember it.
The Sisters of the Bluff moved their spindle, and Morwen of Glenmoril went after it alone.

objectives.text: Hold 3 more fallen stars
Hold the Heart-Star

outcomes.text: You held three more fallen stars and the Heart-Star besides, and the covens' web lost its brightest strand.
You held three more fallen stars, and the covens' web lost a strand with each.
Morwen's raven stopped coming, and the covens sang again.

objectives.text: Tell Morwen of Glenmoril at __glenmoril_ what the spindle is worth
Sell the spindle to _mage_ of the Mages Guild at _hall_ in __hall_
Take the spindle to _priest_, a priest of Arkay, at _temple_ in __temple_

branches.text: What is the Bluff's spindle of starlit thread worth?

choices.text: Burn it in Hircine's fire
Sell it to the Mages Guild
Take it to the priests of Arkay

outcomes.text: You burned the covens' spindle in Hircine's fire, and the starlight went back where it came from. Glenmoril will not forget it.
You sold the covens' spindle to the Mages Guild, who paid well and will want to know how it was made.
You took the covens' spindle to the priests of Arkay, and they cut its thread through.
Morwen of Glenmoril settled the spindle's fate without you.

objectives.text: Turn a Weir Key, raise an Elite Breach and take its first Court
Find Corvane Tull at _tavern_ in __tavern_

outcomes.text: You took the first Court of the torn halls, and met the last of the Battlespire's last class.
Corvane Tull left _tavern_, and no one saw which way he went.

objectives.text: Take three Redoubts of an Elite Breach from the Kyn
Tell Corvane Tull at _tavern_ in __tavern_

outcomes.text: Three more of the Battlemages' torn halls were taken back from the Kyn who stayed Dagon's.
Corvane Tull left _tavern_, and no one saw which way he went.

objectives.text: Take a Valkynaz's Redoubt, which is every fifth Court of the torn halls
Tell Corvane Tull at _tavern_ in __tavern_

outcomes.text: A warrior duke of Dagon's council fell in the Battlemages' own halls. Corvane Tull called it a beginning.
Corvane Tull left _tavern_, and no one saw which way he went.

objectives.text: Hear Corvane Tull's account at _tavern_ in __tavern_
Tell Corvane what to tell the Empire of the Secretary who surrendered the keys

branches.text: What should Corvane tell the Empire of the Secretary who surrendered the Spire's keys?

choices.text: The truth: the keys were given, and why
The mercy asked of him: let the keys have been taken

outcomes.text: Corvane wrote the whole truth of 3E 398 for the Empire, and dated the page today at last.
Corvane granted the old Secretary his mercy, and gave you his Battlemage's blade as his last gift.
Corvane Tull left _tavern_ with his account unwritten.

objectives.text: Ride the Sky-Ketch's anchor-lift up from the fields east of Daggerfall
Tell Imrah Bel-Tavir what is on her deck, at _tavern_ in __tavern_

outcomes.text: You stood on the deck of the Rourken sky-ketch, and told an antiquarian of Sentinel what her book had only guessed.
Imrah Bel-Tavir went home to Sentinel, and left no word.

objectives.text: Set an aether cell in the Sky-Ketch's engine or a resonator with your own hands
Tell Imrah Bel-Tavir at _tavern_ in __tavern_

outcomes.text: You fed the Sky-Ketch with your own hands, and Imrah Bel-Tavir gave you her book on the Rourken's guns.
Imrah Bel-Tavir went home to Sentinel, and left no word.

objectives.text: Cross the Sailwalk to the Sky-Ketch's bridge and still the Tonal Warden
Tell Imrah Bel-Tavir at _tavern_ in __tavern_

outcomes.text: The Sky-Ketch's steersman fell at her helm, and her master's cabin opened.
Imrah Bel-Tavir went home to Sentinel, and left no word.

objectives.text: Hear what Imrah Bel-Tavir read in the lodestone, at _tavern_ in __tavern_
Tell Imrah who should hear what the Sky-Ketch follows

branches.text: Who should hear that the Sky-Ketch's lodestone answers the Brass God?

choices.text: The Mages Guild: write to Ysolde Marnhel
No one: burn the chart

outcomes.text: Imrah wrote to Ysolde Marnhel of the Mages Guild, and hung a Rourken tuning-charm about your neck.
Imrah burned her chart of the Ketch's course, and gave you the steersman's own hammer.
Imrah Bel-Tavir went home to Sentinel, her question unanswered.
